nodes.name: Arc melting of master alloy
nodes.procedure: The Ti50Al48Mo2 master alloys were prepared from pure Ti (99.999%), Al (99.999%), and Mo (99.999%) in an arc-melting furnace under a protective argon atmosphere using a tungsten electrode. Because the melting points of Al (933 K), Ti (1941 K), and Mo (2893 K) are quite different, Ti and Mo were melted together first, then Al was melted in alloys, and the melting process was repeated six times to guarantee uniform elemental combination. The mass losses after arc melting were -0.3%.
nodes.source_text: The Ti50Al48Mo2 master alloys were prepared from pure Ti (99.999%), Al (99.999%), and Mo (99.999%) in an arc-melting furnace under a protective argon atmosphere using a tungsten electrode... The mass losses after arc melting were -0.3%.

nodes.name: Electromagnetic levitation rapid solidification
nodes.procedure: Before the EML experiments, the vacuum degree was guaranteed to be less than 2×10^-4 and 10^5 Pa high-purity argon was introduced. The sample with 1 g mass was levitated by electromagnetic force and superheated at about 100 K by high-frequency induction and then cooled by flowing helium gas to obtain high undercooling.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals dendrite morphology evolution from irregular dendrites at ΔT=50 K to refined structures at higher undercoolings, as shown in Fig. 2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The microstructure evolution of Ti50Al48Mo2 alloy solidified at different undercoolings is shown in Fig. 2.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM analysis at ΔT = 50 K and 253 K reveals B2 phase crystal planes (00-1) and (010), HAADF images, and EDS elemental maps showing Mo-rich B2 phase and homogeneous solute distribution at high undercooling.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The phases and crystalline structure of alloys at ΔT = 50 and 253 K were studied by FEI Themis Z correction transmission electron microscopy (TEM).

properties.description: High-magnification SEM with red arrows indicating nanostructures

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping shows Mo enrichment and Al depletion in B2 phase at ΔT = 50 K, and homogeneous Ti, Al, Mo distribution at ΔT = 253 K.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Combined with the corresponding diffraction pattern of the B2 phase in the TEM analysis (Fig. 3(c)), the crystal planes are (00-1) and (010) respectively. According to the high-angle annular dark field (HAADF) TEM micrographs with the corresponding energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental maps (Fig. 3(b, d–f)), Mo is rich and Al is depleted in the B2 phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS Nyquist plots show incomplete semicircles with increasing capacitive loop diameters (R_ct-f from 0.75×10^6 Ω cm² at ΔT=50 K to 1.52×10^6 Ω cm² at ΔT=253 K) indicating improved passivation film resistance with undercooling.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As Fig. 5(a) shows, all Nyquist plots exhibit incomplete semicircles... The diameter of the capacitive loop reflects the corrosion resistance of the passivation film on the alloy surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves show wider passive regions at higher undercooling; E_corr improves from -0.218 V_SCE (i_corr=1.539×10^{-6} A cm^{-2}) at ΔT=50 K to -0.043 V_SCE (i_corr=1.168×10^{-6} A cm^{-2}, E_pit=0.550 V_SCE) at ΔT=253 K.
